name: Why is my water pressure low in my entire house?

mainEntity.name: Why is my water pressure low in my entire house?

acceptedAnswer.text: Low water pressure throughout your home often indicates a main water supply issue or a problem with your home's plumbing system. Common causes include partially closed main water shut-off valves, issues with the municipal water supply, or a failing pressure regulator. Older homes might experience low pressure due to galvanized pipes corroding and narrowing over time, restricting water flow. A professional plumber can diagnose the exact cause by checking the main valve, pressure regulator, and inspecting your pipes.
